🛒NUT DEMAND
BalanceMarketsU.S. trendRWASources
🛒 RWA · Consumption / disappearance

Where the crop disappears into use.

Trade records movement. Demand records absorption. This page follows nuts to the point where production, imports and inventories become domestic consumption.

3.69 lbU.S. tree nuts/person · 2016 [1]
410k MTEU almond use · MY2024/25 [2]
375k MTU.S. almond use · MY2024/25 [2]
1.616M MTGlobal almond use · MY2024/25 [2]
Demand is not importsA country can consume what it grows, imports, or draws from stocks.

The analytical object is the supply-use balance, not an importer leaderboard.

01 · BALANCE

The demand equation

USDA FAS balances allow domestic consumption to be reconciled against production, trade and stock changes.

Production+Imports−Exports− ΔStocks=Domestic use
Method: FAS tree-nut balances are marketing-year series and often use shelled/kernel-equivalent bases. Reconcile period and product state before comparing to customs data.
02 · MARKETS

Almond demand, MY2024/25

The EU and U.S. form the largest consumption blocks in the October 2024 FAS balance, followed by India and China.

03 · U.S. TREND

Consumption moved materially higher

ERS loss-adjusted food availability is a proxy for consumption, best used for long-run direction.

Per person in 2016. [1]

Other nuts≈1 lb

Cashews, Brazil nuts, chestnuts, pine nuts and mixes in 2016. [1]

04 · RWA

Demand is the exit side of collateral.

Inventory is financeable only if buyers exist at sufficient depth. Demand data informs off-take, depletion, destination concentration and liquidation assumptions.

Off-take depthAnnual market absorption.
ConcentrationDependence on large markets.
TurnoverStocks relative to use.
Price sensitivityBridge to Nut Inflation.

Public-data boundary

Official data are strong at country/commodity level but weaker on retail vs foodservice vs ingredient shares, named buyers, and nuts embedded inside composite foods. Those should be labeled estimates or omitted unless a primary source exists.

Sources

Data registry

Reporting period and product basis stay explicit. Marketing-year balances are not silently mixed with calendar-year customs flows.

[1] USDA ERS · Almonds lead increase in tree nut consumption ↗Loss-adjusted U.S. per-capita food availability; 1970–2016.
[2] USDA FAS · Tree Nuts: World Markets and Trade · October 2024 ↗Almond supply/distribution tables through MY2024/25; metric tons, shelled basis.
[3] USDA FAS · Production, Supply and Distribution Online ↗Official downloadable global supply-use dataset for automated updates.
[4] USDA FAS · European Union Tree Nuts Annual 2025 ↗EU demand and food-processing context.
